subject: Re: Follow-up: Model fit & tool-calling evals (Avery Analytics)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Gupta <sam.gupta@averyai.com>, Priya Shah <priya@averyanalytics.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Model fit & tool-calling evals (Avery Analytics)

Hi Sam / Priya,

Great to meet you both this morning — thanks for the 45-minute discovery. Quick recap / recommended next steps from our side: 

1) Summary of needs (what I heard)
- Primary use: automated policy summarization and routing for internal ops tickets (short-to-medium context, JSON structured output required)
- Latency target: 200-400ms p95 on single-request inference for batched routing calls
- Accuracy: high schema compliance for JSON outputs; firm retry semantics for function/tool calling
- Data sensitivity: PII in prompts; prefer VPC/private deployment for production

2) Model & eval recommendations (initial)
- Start with: redwood-compact-13b-q4 (balanced latency/cost, strong structured-output behavior)
- If higher quality needed: redwood-bison-14b / redwood-owl-35b (higher cost, better few-shot structured fidelity)
- For strict JSON schema enforcement we recommend running structured-output evals with our function-calling harness (we can run on a sample of ~500 prompts)

3) Benchmarks & artifacts I’m attaching / linking:
- prompt set: avery_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (attached) — 120 sample prompts covering happy/path/error cases
- benchmark summary: model_benchmarks_summary.pdf (attached) — preliminary latency and token-cost estimates for the suggested models
- shared drive with full evals: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cBenchmarks

4) Risks / quality concerns
- We flagged potential regression modes: truncated JSON on long outputs, incorrect typing for nested fields, and inconsistent retry behavior for partially completed function calls. Our eval will measure schema compliance, rerun safety, and idempotency of tool calls.

5) Proposed next steps
- Avery: confirm 100 representative prompts for a focused structured-output smoke test (can use attached v1 as starting point)
- Redwood: we’ll run a 500-prompt structured-output eval (JSON schema compliance + tool-calling reliability) and share results within 5 business days
- Schedule technical deep dive: Rishi (solutions engineer) to lead — options: Thu 5/6 09:00-10:00 PT or Fri 5/7 11:00-12:00 PT

I’m looping in Rishi (SE) and Aditya (Applied ML) to scope the eval and set expectations on deliverables. Let me know which deep-dive slot works and if you want us to run the smaller smoke test first.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0118

Attachment stubs: avery_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (jsonl, 120 rows), model_benchmarks_summary.pdf

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying Qs: 

- Can you confirm that redwood-compact-13b-q4 supports function/tool calling with at-least-once vs at-most-once semantics? Our infra needs idempotent retries for webhook-style tool invocations.
- For JSON schema compliance: do you run strict validation (error on schema mismatch) or do you report a confidence/score? We’d like to see a per-prompt breakdown so we can triage failure modes.
- Timeline: if you run the 500-prompt eval, will that include the schema+retry tests you mentioned, and can you include example failing outputs?

Also, please include Rishi on the deep-dive — happy to do Fri 5/7 11:00-12:00 PT. I can share a short doc with our required schema and some examples this afternoon.

Best,
Sam
Head of Product\Avery Analytics
sam.gupta@averyai.com

Hi Sam — great, Fri 5/7 11:00-12:00 PT is on our side.

Quick answers / what we’ll do for the 500-prompt eval:
- Function/tool calling semantics: our runtime supports configurable invocation policies. For this eval we’ll test both (a) at-least-once with idempotency tokens and (b) at-most-once behavior using our built-in deduplication window. We’ll include measured failure/retry scenarios and recommendations on integration patterns.
- JSON schema compliance: we run a structured-output harness that validates model responses against your provided JSON Schema. Outputs are scored per-prompt: (pass/fail), J-schema confidence (0-1), and normalized edit-distance to the expected canonical output. We’ll surface example failures and categorize them (truncation, type mismatch, extra fields).
- Deliverables & timing:
  - Smoke test (100 prompts you confirm): 1 business day (quick pass/fail + top 10 failures)
  - Full eval (500 prompts): 5 business days, includes per-prompt CSV (attached: structured_output_eval_results.csv), aggregated summary PDF, and suggested model/profile (quantization/batching) for your SLOs

Attachments we are providing in the run: structured_output_eval_results.csv (example format), model_benchmarks_summary.pdf. Aditya will run the structured-output harness on the sample you send and produce the per-prompt artifacts.

Rishi — can you coordinate the deep-dive invite and confirm what our SE will need from Avery (schema + representative prompts + a short call to go over integration constraints)?

Sam / Priya — please drop the schema in reply or share the Drive doc. I’ve added our HubSpot deal for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345/AVY-2027-0421

Thanks,
